about: measure contests of 2024 in North Dakota, in the layout of plan/PLAN.md section 3 with the fields data/README.md adds (D3). Built by pipeline/local_medsl.py from pipeline/intake/medsl_precinct.py's cache.

medsl.name: MIT Election Data and Science Lab, Precinct-Level Returns 2024 by Individual State, Harvard Dataverse doi:10.7910/DVN/NYTPDU, version 1.0
medsl.note: precinct returns compiled by MEDSL from each state's official sources (named per state in its README); added up to the contest by pipeline/intake/medsl_precinct.py, files 2024-nd-precinct-general.csv

model.name: the model's own forecast, method D3-v1.1
model.note: each year forecast from a fit on earlier years only; no polls are used

nara.name: National Archives, Electoral College Results (the sitting president's party)
nara.licence: US federal public record; no licence printed

question.title: Proposition Related To Terminology Describing Public Institutions

threshold.rule: majority of votes cast upon the measure
threshold.citation: N.D. Const. art. III, sec. 8 (and sec. 9)
threshold.quote: If a majority of votes cast upon an initiated or a referred measure are affirmative, it shall be deemed enacted.
threshold.matched: the source's title does not give the type; every rule read for the state's measures (but its convention question) sets this threshold

p.under: the model's own (D3-v1.1), like past measures
p.note: this route's back-test of statewide measures shows more near-even finishes than it forecast (11 against 6.8 within 1 point of ½, and 10 against 6.2 within 20,000 votes, 2018 to 2024), so p may be low
